lens: Prospective client — recovery and retry; simulated AI lens
reason: The offer is understandable: student-led, pro-bono, semester-long work with a 6–8-person team, a responsive client contact and jointly scoped confidentiality. The supplied homepage captures show coherent Precision Instrument hierarchy and prominent inquiry actions. Partnership descriptions honestly distinguish organization information from unpublished MECG results. However, the inquiry recovery path can misstate uncertain delivery and erase edits made while sending. These source-confirmed weaknesses prevent world-class agreement from this seat. The logged client journey proves only intercepted success, not actual delivery or observed client success; hold the release acceptance decision pending recovery fixes and integration evidence.

findings.evidence: The contact route sends without an idempotencyKey. Email timeout/network exceptions return delivered:false; the route and browser then assert the message could not be sent and suggest email instead. A provider may already have accepted the message before its acknowledgement is lost.
findings.userImpact: A client cannot distinguish failed delivery from unknown delivery; retrying or using email can duplicate the inquiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a stable inquiry identifier and provider idempotency key for retries; distinguish unknown acknowledgement from definitive rejection and preserve the message. Add interrupted-acknowledgement contact coverage.

findings.evidence: FormData is captured before fetch. Only the submit button is disabled while sending; all fields remain editable. Any successful response calls form.reset() unconditionally.
findings.userImpact: Details added while waiting are absent from the submitted payload and then erased under a success message.
findings.suggestedFix: Lock the submitted fields while sending, or preserve edits that differ from the captured payload and clearly identify what was sent. Verify using a delayed response and an intervening edit.

findings.evidence: The limiter distinguishes unavailable internally, but its boolean wrapper returns false for outages. Contact maps false to 429 and “Too many messages. Try again later.”
findings.userImpact: A first-time client during a database/limiter outage is incorrectly blamed for excess messages and receives no fallback in the error itself.
findings.suggestedFix: Use checkRateLimitStatus, return a retryable service-unavailable response for outages, and include the existing board-email fallback. Test outage separately from actual limiting.

notVerified: No staging, hosted contact delivery, mailbox receipt, reply timing, or authenticated integration was exercised. The client browser test intercepts /api/contact with {ok:true}; API unit tests mock email and rate limiting.
No approved case-study outcomes or project artifacts are supplied; the empty public fallback and publication fixture do not establish consulting quality.
